name: Banded Pull-Apart
description: A simple but highly effective rear deltoid, rhomboid, and rotator cuff exercise performed by pulling a resistance band apart horizontally at chest height. The pull-apart is frequently used as a warm-up, postural corrective exercise, and high-volume accessory for upper back and shoulder health.

execution.starting_position: Stand tall holding a resistance band with both hands at chest height, arms extended forward, hands shoulder-width apart.
execution.setup_instructions: Select a light to medium resistance band. Hold it with palms facing down or facing each other.
steps: Step 1: Keep the arms relatively straight (elbows soft, not locked).
Step 2: Pull the band apart by moving both hands outward and backward.
Step 3: Continue until the band touches or nearly touches the chest, squeezing the rear delts and rhomboids.
Step 4: Return slowly to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the pull apart. Inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Using a band that is too heavy, causing the arms to bend excessively
Moving through too fast without feeling the rear delt contraction
safety_considerations: This exercise should be performed for higher reps (15-25) with a light band for best results
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension of the band behind the chest at the back position.
coaching_cues: Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the end
